strengths: Novel application of TabPFN to RL with in-context learning for Q-value prediction, opening a new research direction for prior-fitted networks in RL

Honest and thorough discussion of theoretical limitations—clearly identifies how bootstrapped labels, non-i.i.d. transitions, and non-stationary visitation distributions violate TabPFN's training assumptions

Principled formalization of context size limitations for ICL RL methods and four well-motivated truncation strategies (Latest Trajectories, Naive Deduplication, Embeddings Deduplication, Reward Variance)
Clear algorithmic presentation with well-specified Algorithm 1 and comprehensive implementation details including hyperparameters and reward shaping functions
Thorough background section and good positioning relative to related work on meta-RL, ICL, and transformer-based RL
weaknesses: Critical dependency on reward shaping: Paper explicitly acknowledges method fails on sparse rewards, yet all three environments require custom reward shaping, undermining claims of being a general gradient-free RL method

Extremely limited experimental scope: Only three trivial classic control tasks (CartPole, MountainCar, Acrobot); no demonstration on visual, high-dimensional, or truly sparse-reward domains that represent modern RL challenges

Only compared to DQN; missing comparisons to other gradient-free methods (Evolution Strategies) and relevant meta-RL baselines (RL², Algorithm Distillation, OmniRL) making it impossible to assess relative merit

Hyperparameter sensitivity contradicts main positioning: Despite claims of avoiding extensive tuning, Figure 3 and ablations show substantial sensitivity to percentile refit, ε decay, initial ε, and context budget; different hyperparameters used per environment

No theoretical explanation for why method works despite violating TabPFN's training assumptions—paper identifies the problem but provides no analysis of generalization capacity or convergence properties
Inference cost analysis missing: O(N²) attention complexity with B=8096 could be prohibitively expensive; no wall-clock time comparison with DQN to justify gradient-free claims
Unclear practical advantage: Paper doesn't articulate when practitioners should use TabPFN-RL over DQN, which is faster, more scalable, and mature; no guidance on method applicability
Acknowledged inability to scale to visual inputs, sparse rewards, or challenging benchmarks (Montezuma's Revenge) severely limits significance for modern RL applications

strengths: Novel idea: Applying pre-trained TabPFN transformer to gradient-free RL through in-context learning is creative and well-motivated conceptually

Honest discussion of limitations: The paper thoroughly acknowledges fundamental issues (prior mismatch, bootstrapped labels, distribution shift, sparse reward failure, reward shaping dependence), demonstrating research integrity
Theoretical analysis: Insightful discussion of why TabPFN should theoretically fail but empirically works, surfacing the generalization capacity of transformer-based ICL
Context truncation strategies: Addresses continual learning problem when context is full, proposing four different truncation operators with empirical evaluation
Comprehensive ablations: Sensitivity analysis across multiple hyperparameters (percentile threshold, epsilon decay, context size) with multiple seeds
weaknesses: CRITICAL: Severely limited experimental scope - only 3 trivial classic control environments (CartPole, MountainCar, Acrobot). These are toy problems solved decades ago and do not validate applicability of a deep RL method

CRITICAL: Heavy reliance on hand-crafted reward shaping for all environments directly contradicts core motivation of reducing hyperparameter sensitivity and engineering burden. Authors acknowledge poor performance on sparse rewards

CRITICAL: Contradicts main claims about hyperparameter tuning - requires extensive per-environment hyperparameter tuning (different ε: 0.95/0.7/0.7, ε decay: 0.9955/0.99/0.99, context sizes: 200/200/128). Authors admit 'we cannot guarantee these are optimal'

Missing critical comparisons: Only compares to DQN (2013), ignoring modern baselines (PPO, SAC) and other gradient-free methods (Evolution Strategies, cited but not benchmarked). No comparison with related meta-RL (Algorithm Distillation, OmniRL) despite being central to motivation

Marginal empirical improvements: Figure 1 shows TabPFN-RL achieves comparable (not superior) performance to DQN with overlapping error bars. No statistical significance testing. Improvement claims are overstated

Computational cost unaddressed: O(N²) inference complexity acknowledged but never measured empirically. No wall-clock time comparisons with DQN. For large context B, inference cost could exceed training cost of gradient methods, undermining efficiency claims

Weak theoretical contributions: 'Theoretical limitations' section merely formalizes obvious constraint (context budget limit). Context truncation methods are ad-hoc heuristics without principled justification. Why these specific strategies? Why 95th percentile?
No ablation without reward shaping: Critical question unanswered - how does TabPFN-RL perform without manual reward engineering? This should be the primary experiment

Insufficient evaluation methodology: Only 250 episodes (very short), no sample efficiency analysis, no investigation of scaling properties, missing comparisons with emergence of gradient-free approaches

Questionable practical advantage: Unclear why practitioners should use TabPFN-RL over mature methods. Not faster (inference cost), not sample efficient (requires initialization), not hyperparameter-free (requires tuning), only works on toy problems

strengths: Novel and creative repurposing of TabPFN as a Q-function approximator, opening a new research direction for gradient-free RL with foundation models

Intellectually honest theoretical analysis of why TabPFN-RL should fail despite prior mismatch, clearly formalizing violations of i.i.d. assumptions from bootstrapped labels, non-i.i.d. episode transitions, and distribution shift

Valuable contribution identifying and formalizing the context size limitation problem for all ICL RL algorithms, with four proposed truncation strategies that could benefit the broader ICL RL community
Strong reproducibility with detailed implementation details, specific hyperparameters, reward shaping functions, and accessible hardware requirements
Commendable acknowledgment and discussion of significant limitations including sparse reward performance, quadratic inference costs, hyperparameter sensitivity, and scalability constraints
weaknesses: Critically limited experimental evaluation: only 3 simple classic control environments tested without comparison to gradient-free baselines (Evolution Strategies, KNN-TD) or modern RL algorithms (only 2013 DQN baseline), and no comparison to other ICL RL methods (Algorithm Distillation, RL2, OmniRL) despite extensive discussion

All three environments require manual, environment-specific reward shaping, directly contradicting the motivation of reducing hyperparameter tuning; this dependency is acknowledged but not adequately addressed in significance
Sparse reward performance explicitly stated as poor with no systematic investigation or proposed solutions, despite being critical for RL applicability

Strong hyperparameter sensitivity despite claims: ablations show sensitivity to initial ε (0.5-0.95), ε decay (0.8-0.999), context budget B (256-8096), and percentile refit; different hyperparameters required per environment contradicts 'no extensive tuning' claim
Quadratic inference cost O(N²) acknowledged but never quantified against claimed benefits; unclear whether quadratic cost outweighs backprop savings and prevents scaling

No statistical significance testing provided; Figure 1 shows high variance with shaded regions but no confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical tests to assess if performance differences are meaningful

Severely limited scope: evaluation only on low-dimensional toy problems with 250 episodes each; no visual domains, continuous control, or challenging environments tested; no evidence of scaling beyond classic control

Weak theoretical analysis of generalization: the claim that TabPFN exhibits greater generalization than explicitly trained on is speculative without formal convergence guarantees, sample complexity analysis, or bounds on generalization

Context truncation strategies are heuristic-based with limited theoretical justification; only Naive De-duplication clearly outperforms baselines with insufficient analysis of when/why each method succeeds
Missing computational cost analysis: no wall-clock timing comparisons between TabPFN-RL inference and DQN training, making efficiency claims impossible to verify

strengths: Novel perspective on RL via reduction to in-context regression using FQI, providing a conceptually clean framework
Comprehensive experimental methodology with 10 seeds per environment and detailed ablation studies on hyperparameters and context engineering
Honest discussion of limitations including task-prior mismatch, sparse reward challenges, and computational complexity
Well-grounded in established theory (FQI from 2007) with clear instantiation via ICR oracle
Good reproducibility documentation with implementation details, hyperparameter specifications, and reward shaping functions in appendix
weaknesses: Fundamental task-prior mismatch unresolved: TabPFN trained on i.i.d. data but FQI produces non-stationary, bootstrapped targets—described as 'unexpected robustness' but no theoretical analysis or characterization of failure modes provided
Extensive reward shaping required for all environments contradicts foundation model philosophy; sparse reward performance is poor, undermining generality claims
Extremely limited experimental scope: only 3 toy classic control environments with low-dimensional states; no high-dimensional, vision-based, or diverse task evaluations

Claimed hyperparameter reduction not substantiated: method has ε-schedule parameters, context budget B, percentile refit α, FQI iterations, and multiple context engineering strategies, with Figure 7 showing substantial sensitivity
Theory-practice gap on FQI: best performance at α=0.1 iterations contradicts theory suggesting α≈1; contradiction acknowledged but not resolved, indicating unexplained behavioral deviations
Computational efficiency not demonstrated: quadratic transformer complexity mentioned but no wall-clock time comparisons with baselines; Figures 4-5 lack baseline timings
Modest novelty: primarily combines existing components (classical FQI algorithm with existing TabPFN backbone); context engineering methods are ad-hoc heuristics without principled justification
High sensitivity to ICR backbone revealed by Section 4.3 (TabICL needed for sparse rewards) contradicts robustness and generality claims
Missing critical diagnostic experiments: no evaluation without reward shaping, no computational benchmarking versus DQN, no analysis of Bellman error reduction, no failure mode characterization

strengths: Novel conceptual contribution: The reduction from RL to in-context regression provides an interesting perspective on foundation models for RL without domain-specific pre-training
Well-presented and organized paper with comprehensive implementation details, ablation studies, and an informative appendix
Creative application of TabPFN to RL through FQI with thoughtful context engineering approaches (naive de-duplication, embeddings de-duplication, reward variance)
Honest acknowledgment of limitations including sparse reward failures, reward shaping requirements, and scalability challenges
Demonstrates generality of framework by showing different ICR backbones (TabPFN vs. TabICL) perform better in different settings
weaknesses: Fundamental prior-data mismatch remains unresolved: TabPFN trained on i.i.d. data but FQI generates non-stationary, bootstrapped targets with temporal correlations and distribution shift. No theoretical analysis explains why the method works despite these violations

Empirical divergence from FQI theory unexplained: Best performance at α=0.1 contradicts theory predicting K≈α/(1-γ)≈1. This discrepancy suggests potential misalignment between theoretical framework and actual method operation

Critical reliance on reward shaping: Method fails on sparse rewards without modification; requires task-specific shaped rewards (different for each of 3 environments). This undermines claims of generality and foundation model applicability

No demonstrated performance advantage: ICR-RL is merely competitive with DQN (often matching or worse on Acrobot), providing no compelling reason to adopt the more complex approach with reward engineering requirements

Severely limited experimental scope: Only 3 classic control tasks with ≤4D state spaces; 250 episodes; no high-dimensional evaluation despite motivation. Authors acknowledge 'scaling to high-dimensional tasks is non-trivial and has not yet been tested'

Computational efficiency claims undermined: Quadratic transformer complexity acknowledged as 'challenge, slowing ICR-RL training and inference'; no wall-clock timing comparisons despite claiming gradient-free computation as key advantage

Significant hyperparameter sensitivity despite simplicity claims: Exploration schedules (Figures 7, 9), context budget, percentile refit parameter all substantially affect performance, comparable to complexity of tuning gradient-based methods
Lack of statistical rigor: No confidence intervals or significance tests reported; Figure 2 shows overlapping regions; unclear if performance differences are statistically meaningful

Missing critical analysis: (1) Why does α=0.1 outperform theoretical predictions? (2) How does prior-data mismatch impact performance? (3) What does TabPFN learn from synthetic regression that transfers to RL? (4) Why do different ICR models needed for different tasks?
Limited scope of comparison: No empirical evaluation against OmniRL or other recent in-context RL methods despite acknowledgment in related work

strengths: Elegant reduction from RL to regression via FQI with clear motivation and well-organized presentation
Practical context engineering contributions (naive de-duplication, reward variance, etc.) with solid empirical validation showing 40% runtime reduction
Comprehensive experimental methodology including multiple ablation studies across context size, FQI iterations, and exploration schedules with proper statistical reporting (10 seeds)
Honest treatment of limitations (prior-data mismatch, sparse rewards, quadratic complexity) and useful framework comparison table positioning the work relative to related methods

Interesting empirical finding that TabPFN generalizes zero-shot to RL despite training on different data distribution, supporting the broader hypothesis that regression FM improvements could translate to RL FM improvements
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope: only 3 toy environments (CartPole, MountainCar, Acrobot), all low-dimensional—no high-dimensional tasks, Atari, MuJoCo, or robotics benchmarks despite claiming these as future work

Fundamental practical limitation inadequately emphasized: method requires reward shaping for all tested environments and performs poorly on sparse rewards, directly contradicting the paper's core claim about gradient-free learning without extensive domain-specific engineering

Incomplete theoretical understanding: (1) prior-data mismatch between TabPFN (i.i.d.) and FQI (non-stationary, bootstrapped targets) is acknowledged but unresolved with only vague claims of 'unexpected robustness'; (2) Figure 8 shows α=0.1 empirically optimal versus α≈1 from theory, a significant discrepancy with no explanation

Hyperparameter sensitivity contradicts simplicity claims: ablations reveal high sensitivity to ε-schedule parameters (λ, ε₀ in Figure 9), context budget B (Figure 7), percentile thresholds, and number of FQI iterations—undermining the narrative about eliminating extensive hyperparameter search

No computational cost analysis: no wall-clock time comparisons with baselines despite quadratic transformer complexity being mentioned as limitation; Figure 5 shows relative runtime but without absolute times or per-environment details
Competitive but not superior performance to DQN raises unclear practical advantage; outperforms less stable PPO/TRPO but matches rather than exceeds the standard baseline

Sparse reward limitation inadequately addressed: Figure 6 (TabICL vs TabPFN) reveals backbone-dependence and suggests framework weakness, but analysis is minimal; unclear how robust this approach is across different data regimes

Overstated claims about 'gradient-free method requiring no additional training' when method requires careful tuning of multiple hyperparameters as shown in ablations; 'zero-shot' is misleading since many forward passes needed to build context
